title: Rabbit's Foot Minstrels and Brown Skin Models
summary: Jones dislikes minstrel shows, talks about the Rabbit's Foot in 1940, bandleader Hosey Sapp, and how he got the comedian spot in New Orleans theaters.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

When they were trying to find a comedian, I happened to be in New Orleans at the time at the palace. I stayed there seven weeks at the palace doing a single. And they couldn't find nobody to hold down the spot. But they had a fellow there named Jazz Richardson. He was a mighty great comedian at the time, but somehow, I don't know where they let him go, I think. I don't know where they didn't do something right or something wrong, anyhow, they let him go. I said, well, they came to New Orleans and were looking for a comic, and they're lucky enough to find me there, because I had laid where Rapsford had closed. We closed the show, St. Joe, Mississippi.
